title: MCP (Model Context Protocol): how agents reach tools, and where you can stop them
summary: Hold: the data-policy navigation path omits the Settings section named in Microsoft's instructions. The Work IQ policy path also omits the registry tab; the other deterministic pre-check warnings are supported by the documentation.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Block blocks a server across the organisation and disables its tools.
claims.quote: Select Agents > Tools, and then select the Registry tab. ... Select an MCP server from the list to open its overview pane. ... Select Block to restrict the server across your organization ... Blocking an MCP server disables all the tools it exposes.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for blocking a registry MCP server is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/graph MCP server registry block unblock individual tools approval requests API. Opened manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers and develop-mcp; the latter removes the block command. The Enterprise MCP service-principal example is not this registry control.

claims.claim: Agents > Tools > Registry > MCP server > Tools > Enabled / Disabled toggle > Save controls individual tools on supported servers.
claims.quote: Select the Tools tab. The list shows every tool the server exposes, along with its description and an Enabled or Disabled toggle. ... Turn individual tools on or off as needed. ... Select Save to apply your changes

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for blocking an individual registry MCP tool is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/graph MCP server registry block unblock individual tools approval requests API. Opened manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers and develop-mcp; reviewed Azure API Management search results. No equivalent registry tool-toggle call was documented.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for approving MCP registration requests is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/graph MCP server registry block unblock individual tools approval requests API. Opened manage-plugins-skills-mcp-servers and develop-mcp; the CLI reference says develop-mcp approve is no longer included and directs administrators to the admin center.

claims.claim: Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access governs publisher types, including connectors and MCP servers.
claims.quote: Agent and plugin access controls which types of agents and plugins, including connectors and MCP servers, are available in your organization. ... go to Agents > Settings > Agent and plugin access.

claims.claim: Agents > Settings > User access controls which users can access agents and plugins, including MCP servers and connectors.
claims.quote: Plugins include tools, MCP servers, connectors, skills, and other AI artifacts. ... Select Agents > Settings > User access to manage your organization's agents and plugins.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for the tenant User access setting is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com "Agent and plugin access" "Graph" "User access". Opened agent-settings and manage-federated-connectors; Graph results concern app-role assignments and agent identities, not this tenant-wide population setting.

claims.where: controls[5].ui; What it is; Governance controls
claims.claim: Copilot > Connectors > Your connections provides a connector's Enable / Disable action and Staged rollout > Add staging.
claims.quote: Enable / Disable | Copilot > Connectors > Your connections ... Limit a connector to specific users or Microsoft Entra ID groups by choosing Add staging in the Staged rollout column.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for federated connector enablement and staged rollout is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: federated connectors enable disable staged rollout Microsoft Graph PowerShell API. Opened federated-connectors-overview and manage-federated-connectors; reviewed custom federated connector and staged-rollout results. None gives an equivalent automation call.

claims.where: controls[6].ui; Governance controls; What to check
claims.claim: Work IQ MCP tenant policy is reached through Agents > Tools > Work IQ MCP > Policy.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Agents > Tools. ... In the tools registry, select Work IQ MCP. ... On the Work IQ MCP details pane, select the Policy tab when it's available.
claims.fix: Include the tab that lists the servers: 'Agents > Tools > Registry > Work IQ MCP > Policy'. Keep the qualification that the Policy tab is available only where the tenant and administrator have access.

claims.claim: No automation equivalent for Work IQ MCP tenant policy is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Work IQ MCP tenant policy settings REST API update policy Allowed Disallowed. Opened policy-governance-mcp and the Work IQ overview; reviewed policy and tool-reference results. They describe settings and validation but publish no policy-update endpoint.

claims.claim: Security > Data and privacy > Advanced connector policies opens the single-environment advanced connector policy experience.
claims.quote: In the navigation pane, select Security. ... In the Security pane, select Data and privacy. ... Select Advanced connector policies.

claims.claim: POST /governance/ruleBasedPolicies?api-version=2024-10-01 creates a policy, then POST /governance/ruleBasedPolicies/<policyId>/environmentGroups/<environmentGroupId>/assignments?api-version=2024-10-01 with {} assigns it.

claims.claim: The data-policy creation path is Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy.
claims.quote: Select Security in the navigation pane. ... In the Security pane, under Settings, select Data and privacy. ... In the Data protection and privacy screen, select the Data policy section. Select + New Policy.
claims.fix: Replace controls[8].ui.path and the corresponding rendered path with 'Security > Settings > Data and privacy > Data policy > + New Policy', retaining https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/prevent-data-loss as the reference.

claims.where: controls[9].ui; What it is; What to check
claims.claim: Dataverse MCP settings and clients are under Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Dataverse Model Context Protocol > Advanced Settings.
claims.quote: Select Manage > Environments. ... Select the Environment Name ... select Settings. Under Settings, select Product > Features. Scroll down to locate Dataverse Model Context Protocol ... Select Advanced Settings.

claims.claim: PATCH <organization URI>/api/data/v9.2/allowedmcpclients(<allowedmcpclientid>) with isenabled false or true disables or enables an individual client.
claims.quote: Entity set path: [organization URI]/api/data/v9.2/allowedmcpclients ... Primary key: allowedmcpclientid ... Operations supported: POSTGETPATCHDELETE ... isenabled | Edm.Boolean | Display name: Is Enabled ... 1 | Yes ... 0 | No

claims.claim: MCP lets Copilot Studio connect agents to external knowledge servers and data sources.
claims.quote: Model Context Protocol (MCP) helps you connect to existing knowledge servers and data sources directly within Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: An MCP server publishes tools and resources that a Copilot Studio agent can access as a client.
claims.quote: Each tool or resource that a connected MCP server publishes is automatically available for use in Copilot Studio. ... Copilot Studio agents can access each tool.

claims.claim: MCP resources are file-like data an agent can read.
claims.quote: Resources: File-like data that an agent can read for more context, such as API responses or file contents

claims.claim: MCP tools are functions a language model can call to perform an action.
claims.quote: Tools: Functions that a language model can call to perform an action

claims.claim: MCP prompts are predefined templates.
claims.quote: Prompts: Predefined prompt templates to accomplish specific tasks

claims.claim: Copilot Studio currently supports MCP tools and resources.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio currently supports MCP tools and resources.

claims.claim: The MCP server supplies tool names, descriptions, inputs and outputs.
claims.quote: The server provides the name, description, inputs, and outputs.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio reflects tools added, updated or removed on an MCP server.
claims.quote: Each tool or resource that a connected MCP server publishes is automatically available for use in Copilot Studio. ... When you update or remove tools and resources on the MCP server, Copilot Studio dynamically reflects these changes.

claims.claim: The standard-harness documentation requires generative orchestration for MCP.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness. ... You must turn on generative orchestration to use MCP.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio supports Streamable transport for MCP.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio supports the Streamable transport type.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio no longer supports SSE for MCP after August 2025.
claims.quote: Copilot Studio no longer supports SSE for MCP after August 2025.

claims.claim: The MCP onboarding wizard offers None, API key and OAuth 2.0 authentication.
claims.quote: Select the authentication type for your MCP server, if applicable. You have three options: None; API key: Configure API key authentication; OAuth 2.0: Configure OAuth 2.0 authentication

claims.claim: Power Platform data policies govern Copilot Studio MCP connectivity, and blocking a connector blocks dependent MCP tools.
claims.quote: Blocking Power Platform connectors also blocks access to tools in connected MCP servers, which rely on Power Platform connectors for connectivity.

claims.claim: Advanced connector policies govern MCP servers within Power Platform at environment or environment-group scope.
claims.quote: You can configure advanced connector policies at the environment group level for bulk deployment or directly on individual environments for targeted governance. ... administrators can see MCP servers listed alongside other connector types and can choose to block an entire MCP server.

claims.claim: Work IQ offers a remote MCP server.
claims.quote: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server, and a REST API.

claims.claim: Federated connectors can create, update or delete data on the user's behalf where the connector exposes those tools.
claims.quote: Where a connector provides the tools, Copilot can also create, update, or delete data in the connected system on the user's behalf.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP provides tools for querying records.
claims.quote: The Dataverse MCP server provides tools for common data operations such as querying records, creating and updating rows, and describing table schemas.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP provides tools for creating and updating rows.
claims.quote: The Dataverse MCP server provides tools for common data operations such as querying records, creating and updating rows, and describing table schemas.

claims.claim: The Copilot connectors overview still calls federated connectors read-only, disagreeing with the federated overview's write-tool documentation.
claims.quote: Federated connectors are read-only; they can search and fetch content but can't write data back.

claims.claim: The Copilot connectors overview announces write actions starting early October 2026.
claims.quote: Write actions will be available starting early October 2026.

claims.claim: Plugin package-level actions are not separate controls for each included component.
claims.quote: These package-level actions aren't separate controls for each included component. ... Copilot Studio and Power Platform can have separate controls for their components and connections.

claims.claim: No licence or meter for the MCP protocol itself is documented as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: Model Context Protocol protocol itself license fee meter Microsoft. Opened agent-extend-action-mcp, billing-credit-overview, the Work IQ overview, Agent 365 service description and Dataverse MCP FAQ. Published charges concern clients, servers or governance, not the protocol itself.

claims.claim: The Agent 365 service description lists tenant-wide tool control as requiring Microsoft 365 E7 / G7 or Agent 365 rather than inclusion with other Microsoft 365 plans.
claims.quote: Included with Microsoft 365 Enterprise, Business, Education, and Front Line Worker plans | Requires Microsoft 365 E7 / G7 or Agent 365 ... Control which tools (including Microsoft MCP servers) agents can access tenant-wide | Microsoft 365 Admin Center | No | Yes | Yes

claims.claim: Tools including MCPs consume Copilot Credits on the Microsoft Copilot harness.
claims.quote: For experiences powered by the Microsoft Copilot harness, Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.claim: Work IQ API usage is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server, and a REST API. Usage is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP is available through usage-based billing.
claims.quote: Work IQ API endpoints include A2A, a remote MCP server, and a REST API. Usage is independent of Microsoft 365 Copilot licensing and available through usage-based billing.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP tools are charged from 15 December 2025 when accessed by AI agents created outside Copilot Studio.
claims.quote: Starting December 15, 2025, Dataverse MCP tools are charged when accessed by AI agents created outside of Microsoft Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: Qualifying Dynamics 365 Premium licences or a Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription licence exempt access to Dynamics 365 data from that charge.
claims.quote: If you have qualifying Dynamics 365 Premium licenses or a Microsoft 365 Copilot User Subscription License (USL), you aren't charged for accessing Dynamics 365 data.

claims.claim: A user needs a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence to see a federated connector.
claims.quote: A user sees a federated connector in Copilot only when all of the following are true: ... The user has a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.claim: Advanced connector policies block MCP servers as a whole and do not provide individual MCP tool control.
claims.quote: As of now, granular control over individual MCP tools (endpoints and actions) within an MCP server isn't available. Blocking the entire MCP server is supported.

claims.claim: Saving or publishing an advanced connector policy enforces a strict allowlist.
claims.quote: ACP enforces a strict allowlist as soon as you save it (single environment) or publish it (environment group): every connector that isn't explicitly allowed is blocked.

claims.claim: Advanced connector policies do not yet support custom connectors.
claims.quote: Custom connectors and HTTP connectors aren't yet supported.

claims.claim: Advanced connector policies do not yet support HTTP connectors.
claims.quote: Custom connectors and HTTP connectors aren't yet supported.

claims.claim: Registry tool-level control is rolling out and supports only specific MCP server types.
claims.quote: Tool-level granular control is rolling out to tenants and supports only specific types of MCP servers registered on Agent 365.

claims.claim: Without tool discovery, individual tools cannot be managed in the registry and the documented alternative is server blocking.
claims.quote: If an MCP server doesn't support tool discovery ... individual tools aren't available to manage. In this case, use Block or allow an MCP server to control the entire server instead.

claims.claim: MCP server blocking is component-level and its effects on dependent plugins and linked connectors depend on the management route.
claims.quote: Blocking an MCP server is a separate component-level action; effects on dependent plugins and linked connectors depend on the applicable management route.

claims.claim: Blocking a plugin leaves associated MCP servers available to other plugins.
claims.quote: Blocking a plugin prevents users from accessing the plugin and any agents that depend on it. Associated MCP servers and connectors remain available to other plugins.

claims.claim: Copilot Studio makes the person connecting a non-Microsoft MCP server responsible for the tools and resources accessed.
claims.quote: When you connect to a non-Microsoft product, including an external MCP server, you're responsible for the tools and resources you access from within Copilot Studio.

claims.claim: Data processed by non-Microsoft services is not subject to Microsoft agreements.
claims.quote: Data processed by non-Microsoft services isn't subject to Microsoft agreements.

claims.claim: Disabling Dataverse MCP stops the tools and agents that rely on it.
claims.quote: Disabling the Dataverse MCP Server stops all tools and agents that rely on it.

claims.claim: Dataverse MCP client allow listing applies only to /api/mcp, not MCP-named custom APIs.
claims.quote: MCP allow listing applies only to the /api/mcp agent entrypoint. MCP-named custom APIs are regular Dataverse APIs and aren't restricted by this setting.

claims.claim: Work IQ MCP policy cannot grant access beyond the signed-in user's existing access.
claims.quote: Policy can't grant access beyond what the signed-in user is already allowed to access.

claims.where: Risks and limits; controls[6].note; What to check
claims.claim: A saved Work IQ MCP policy change can take up to 24 hours to apply.
claims.quote: After you save the setting, it can take up to 24 hours for the policy change to apply across your tenant.

claims.claim: Unblock restores access to a blocked MCP server.
claims.quote: Select Block to restrict the server across your organization, or Unblock to restore access to a previously blocked server.

claims.claim: User access offers All users by default, No users, and Specific users or groups.
claims.quote: The setting has three options: All users - This option is the default. ... No users ... Specific users or groups

claims.claim: The initial Work IQ MCP policy control is tenant-level on or off and can enable supported mutation scenarios.
claims.quote: In the initial release, Work IQ MCP provides tenant-level policy control. ... Administrators can enable supported mutation scenarios through tenant policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center when those capabilities are needed.

claims.claim: The advanced connector policy API host is api.powerplatform.com and its create body has name and ruleSets with ConnectorManagement, version and inputs.AllowedConnectorList.
claims.quote: $apiBaseUrl = "https://api.powerplatform.com" ... An advanced connector policy is a rule-based policy that contains a rule set with the ID ConnectorManagement. That rule set carries a version and its inputs hold an AllowedConnectorList

claims.claim: A single environment is assigned through the policy's /environments/<environmentId>/assignments route.
claims.quote: Invoke-RestMethod -Method Post ` -Uri "$apiBaseUrl/governance/ruleBasedPolicies/$policyId/environments/$environmentId/assignments?api-version=$apiVersion" ` -Headers $headers -ContentType "application/json" -Body "{}"

claims.claim: The Dataverse MCP Copilot Studio client is enabled by default and additional clients must be enabled.
claims.quote: By default, the Microsoft Copilot Studio client for Dataverse MCP is enabled for all environments. You must enable the additional clients in the Power Platform admin center before you can connect to the client.

claims.claim: The Dataverse MCP configuration page requires Power Platform administrator for the listed MCP settings, client enablement, environment groups and connector-policy tasks.
claims.quote: Power Platform administrator role in order to access Dataverse MCP server environment settings, enable allowed MCP clients, create or edit an environment group, and change connector policies.

claims.claim: The tenant-level data-policy procedure requires Power Platform Administrator.
claims.quote: To follow the steps described in this article for tenant-level policies, sign in as a user with the Power Platform Administrator role.

claims.claim: Environment-level data policies need Environment Admin permissions, or System Administrator for environments with Dataverse.
claims.quote: To follow the steps for environment-level policies, you need to have Power Apps Environment Admin permissions. For environments with a Dataverse database, you need to be assigned the System Administrator role instead.

claims.claim: Managing federated connectors requires Global Administrator or Search Administrator.
claims.quote: To manage federated connectors, you need one of the following administrator roles: Global Administrator; Search Administrator

claims.claim: The Dataverse MCP configuration page requires a Managed Environment for managing that server through advanced connector policies.
claims.quote: The environment must be a Managed Environment if you want to manage the Dataverse MCP server through Advanced connector policies.

claims.claim: An environment group's advanced connector policy is under Manage > Environment groups > group > Rules.
claims.quote: select Manage. ... select Environment groups. ... select the environment group where you want to apply the policy. ... Select the Rules tab. ... Select Advanced connector policies.

claims.claim: A federated connector requires an allowed publisher type or an individual connector override.
claims.quote: A user sees a federated connector in Copilot only when all of the following are true: ... The connector's publisher type is allowed in Agent and plugin access, or an admin turned on the connector individually.

claims.claim: A federated connector must be enabled for a user to see it.
claims.quote: A user sees a federated connector in Copilot only when all of the following are true: ... The connector is enabled.

claims.claim: A user must be included in User access to see a federated connector.
claims.quote: A user sees a federated connector in Copilot only when all of the following are true: ... The user is included in User access.

claims.claim: A user must be included in the federated connector's staged rollout to see it.
claims.quote: A user sees a federated connector in Copilot only when all of the following are true: ... The user is included in the connector's staged rollout.

claims.where: Governance controls: How they interact; controls[5].note
claims.claim: Staged rollout cannot extend a connector's audience beyond User access.
claims.quote: Only these users can use any connector. Connector staging can narrow but not widen this population.

claims.claim: Clearing a publisher type sets its existing connectors' staged rollout to No users.
claims.quote: When you clear an option, existing connectors of that type remain visible to admins in Copilot connectors > Your connections, but their staged rollout is set to No users.

claims.claim: Microsoft labels the connector admin-centre tools view Coming soon.
claims.quote: View a connector's tools in the admin center (Coming soon)

claims.claim: The admin-centre connector tools view is not available for all connectors.
claims.quote: Viewing tools in the admin center isn't available for all connectors.

claims.claim: The documented fallback is Microsoft 365 Copilot > Settings > Sources > connector > Write/Delete tools.
claims.quote: If you encounter issues, sign in to Microsoft 365 Copilot with your user account, go to Settings -> Sources, and select the connector. Then expand Write/Delete tools.

claims.quote: Admins can audit activity in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: Individual tool blocking for BYO MCP servers is planned for a future release.
